issues.description: Duplicate "transcriber_error" entry in the error message_type tuple.
issues.detail: The tuple lists "transcriber_error" twice. Harmless at runtime due to set-like membership semantics, but it signals the author didn't audit their own diff. Deduplicate, ideally by lifting the catalog to a module-level frozenset constant.

issues.description: Removing the outer try/except changes disconnect semantics without making them explicit.
issues.detail: The new _receive_messages relies on the websocket async iterator terminating cleanly on disconnect. If the iterator raises (e.g. ConnectionClosed), the exception now propagates uncaught and the previous "connection closed" breadcrumb is gone. Audit the iterator contract, log once at warning on disconnect, and document the new return-vs-raise invariant.

issues.description: Per-error-type logging and message prefixes silently dropped.
issues.detail: The previous code emitted logger.error with category-specific prefixes ("Auth error:", "Quota exceeded:") before push_error. The collapsed branch drops both. Operators grepping logs and downstream consumers parsing prefixes will silently break. Restore a logger.error including message_type and preserve a typed error in push_error.

issues.description: Error-type catalog is data masquerading as control flow.
issues.detail: A 14-element tuple of protocol error types embedded in an elif is a value, not syntax. Lift it to a module-level frozenset (e.g. ELEVENLABS_ERROR_MESSAGE_TYPES) with a comment citing the upstream cookbook, so the taxonomy is auditable in one place and the handler reads as data dispatch.

issues.description: Fallback string "Unknown error - {message_type}" complects type tag with human message.
issues.detail: When data.get('error') is missing, the synthesized string mixes a sentinel phrase with the message_type, forcing downstream consumers to parse it. Push a structured value containing type and error message separately rather than a flattened string.

issues.description: No test covers the disconnect path or the expanded error types.
issues.detail: The core claim of the PR is "the receive loop used to hang on disconnect; now it does not." There is no regression test asserting that, nor any test exercising the broadened error taxonomy. A small unit test feeding a disconnect into the iterator and asserting clean return would lock in the fix.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the fix is directionally correct: removing the outer try/except in _receive_messages addresses a real infinite reconnect loop, and consolidating error branches reduces duplication. However, execution is sloppy in three concrete ways all three reviewers flagged: a duplicated "transcriber_error" entry, silently dropped per-type logging and message prefixes, and an implicit new exception-propagation contract with no replacement breadcrumb on disconnect. The error-type catalog should be lifted to a module-level frozenset constant so data and dispatch are separated. NEEDS-WORK: dedupe, restore a single warning log on disconnect, preserve typed error labeling, lift the catalog, and add at least one disconnect-path test.
